title: Apple Cider Cheddar Chicken Thighs
description: Cider and sage cut through a mellow cheddar gravy for juicy chicken thighs.
equipment: Ninja Crispi, 4-qt glass container and adapter

steps.title: Simmer the sauce
steps.text: Whisk {broth}, {applejuice}, {sage} into the HexClad. Simmer gently for 2 minutes until combined.

steps.title: Thicken
steps.text: Whisk {starch} with {cold}, then stir into the simmering sauce for 1 minute until it coats a spoon.

steps.title: Finish the sauce
steps.text: Remove from the heat and whisk in {cheddar} until evenly incorporated.

steps.title: Prepare the dish
steps.text: Start with the room-temperature 4-qt glass container, no crisper plate. Let sauce cool to lukewarm before adding to the glass. Spread the sauce over the base.

steps.title: Prepare the chicken
steps.text: Unfold {chicken} into an even layer and trim any loose fat.

steps.title: Cook in sauce
steps.text: Nestle the pieces in the sauce in a single layer. Fit the 4-qt adapter and PowerPod and select Bake. Cook for 20–29 minutes, checking the thickest piece early. Finish at 175°F in the center.

steps.title: Serve generously
steps.text: Spoon hot sauce over each serving.

notes: Make ahead: prepare the sauce a day ahead and refrigerate separately. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze cooked portions with sauce, cooled within 2 hours, for up to 2 months. Fridge reheat: cover and warm gently with a spoonful of water to 165°F. Freezer reheat: thaw overnight in the fridge, then reheat covered to 165°F. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For gentler Option B, omit added citrus, vinegar or chile where used. Pass additional heat at the table. Dairy swap: use unsweetened oat milk and equivalent plain dairy-free cheese if needed. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 230 kcal, 27.9 g protein, 6.9 g total carbohydrate, 9.3 g fat, 0.2 g fiber, 206 mg sodium.
